newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Desc diversifies commodity-based business.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Desc diversifies commodity-based business.

text.p: Mexican conglomerate Desc has opened the door for an important engine for growth in its agribusiness division with this week's purchase of Corporacion del Fuerte (Corfuerte), analysts said Thursday.
Desc announced Wednesday it had agreed in principle with shareholders and creditor banks to acquire 80 percent of the operations of food processor Corfuerte.
Arturo D'Acosta, Desc's treasury and financial planning corporate director, told Reuters that Desc would pay out around $70 million if the acquisition is formally approved by authorities.

"For Desc, the proposed acquisition provides an important engine for growth for its agribusiness sector, helping the Mexican conglomerate diversify its agribusiness portfolio from commodity-type food products such as poultry, pork and shrimp and expand into branded processed products..." Bear Steans analysts Santiago Pique and Marc McCarthy said in a report.
Pique and McCarthy added the purchase will also provide Desc with an additional distribution network and a foothold in export-orientated products.

"The transaction is expected to be concluded within the next few weeks and...will be financed with a bridge loan to be replaced with internal cash flow generation, without the need to increase long term debt in Desc's books," they added.
Desc is already a major Mexican player in agribusiness, with a division devoted mainly to hog and poultry farming. It also has divisions for autoparts, chemicals, real estate and consumer products.

"It is, strategically speaking, a good diversification away from the cyclical side of Desc's business," Abaco brokerage analyst Bond Snodgrass told Reuters. The performance of Desc's agribusiness division is often at the whim of international grains prices.
Snodgrass liked the acquisition because it also took Desc's business closer to the consumer and would mean an additional 5.6 percent of revenues in dollar terms than those posted in 1996.
Corfuerte is a leading processor and marketeer of food products, including the Del Fuerte brand tomato pastes, canned vegetables and sauces.
With its La Gloria brand, Corfuerte also has strong market share in corn oil and corn starch. It also has a toehold in the Mexican coffee market with brand names Blason and Latino.
Corfuerte also has exclusive distribution rights in Mexico for Reynolds Metals Co's aluminum foil, J.M. Smucker Co's jams and Celestial Seasoning Inc's teas.

According to Bear Steans, Corfuerte operates six production plants in Mexico and one in California, nine distribution centers in Mexico and three in the U.S. southwest. Corfuerte posted 1996 sales of $85 million, of which 19 percent was exported oriented.
Abaco's Snodgrass said the distribution side of Corfuerte's business could also help out consolidate and expand Desc's agribusiness division.

Snodgrass suggested Desc might even move into branding its poultry business and competing against the likes of Tyson Foods inc in the south of the United States. "Who knows maybe this (acquisition) can help their existing product lines?" he pondered.
